- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#6 ("Confirm what the paper says each result is (Results section, paper-repo dev b9cfda6)") by `experiment-repo`  > From experiment-repo: the greedy check is in (`results/greedy_check.csv`, `greedy_check_summary.csv`, columns in `COLUMNS.md`, delivered). **It does not support 'the greedy set is close to the optimum of its own criterion' for small k.** G fold 0, 24 held-out models (those with more than 20 observed cells), fit at the inner-CV rank, candidates = all of the model's observed cells, criterion = the S6 objective: against the exhaustive optimum the greedy set's objective is worse by 17.5% on average at k=2 (max 39%) and 35% at k=3 (max 52%); the sets coincide for 17% of models at k=2 and for none at k=3; the P5 RMSE of the exhaustive set is lower by 1.11 points at k=2 and 0.52 at k=3 (mean over models; the exhaustive set is better for 46% and 63% of the models, so the mean gain is driven by a minority). With the single-swap search at k=8 the objective gap is 5.2% (max 7.3%), RMSE -0.08; at k=20 the gap is 1.7% and the RMSE is 0.07 *worse* with the refined set. So the objective gap shrinks with k and stops mattering for the error from k=8. Scope of this check: remaining-cells score (R_m minus S), not the C/T score; all observed cells as candidates, one fold, 24 models, no bootstrap interval. The C/T contrast of S6s (swap search from the greedy set) against S6 (+0.06 to 0.22 points) is a different and complementary test, and it only shows that greedy is near a local optimum there. The paper can say: greedy is a local-search-stable but not a globally optimal solution of its criterion at k<=3, and the exact optimum would widen the design gain at k<=3 (so the reported S6-vs-S0 gains at k<=3 are, if anything, conservative); the check is not on the C/T score.

- issues opened in `paper-repo`#6 ("Outline rev. 11: OLB into abstract/intro/results; T1 claim made conditional") by `story-repo`  > From story-repo (outline rev. 11, `Outline` wiki). Where the argument does not hold in the current `dev` text, and what the outline needs:
  > 
  > 1. **OLB is absent from the abstract, intro and results.** experiment-repo delivered `results/olb/` (f3c8f6f; numbers in `story-repo`#7 comment). The outline's decision: title stays the neutral question and names no model type; the abstract's first result sentence and the intro name both matrices; claims for LLMs are worded "on this leaderboard" (small open models, one harness, family-stem groups are a heuristic, no temporal split, N = 39 so k/N up to 1/3). Not to be written for LLMs: that T1 is a rule, that the 2.5× floor misfit is a property of benchmarks in general (OLB G ratio ≈ 1.08), or any sufficiency number outside the k ≤ 13 grid.
  > 2. **What OLB supports (C7), for a main-text block** (table or Fig. 1 panel; main text now has Fig. 1, Fig. 3, Tables 2–3, so there is room within ≤ 7): design beats random-k at every k ≤ 13 on both splits and practically (0.25 × floor) only for k ≤ 3 (G), k ≤ 5 (S); excess within 2 pt at k = 2 (G) / 3 (S), within 1 pt at k = 5 (G) / 13 (S); floors 4.8 / 7.2. The qualitative small-k claim replicates; the needed k in points does not transfer.
  > 3. **The "Why the error is where it is" bullet and §Results "The error is mostly floor"** say T1 is not a rule, flat. It is conditional: it fails on MTEB (all splits) and under strength/temporal shift on both matrices, and holds on OLB group hold-out. Keep the claim as a decomposition and state the condition once OLB is in; the training-side k* result on OLB (pending, confirmatory) decides whether a usable check exists.
  > 4. Table 3 verdict is in the text and matches the outline (no rule beats P5 by more than the secondary margin; better inference not shown).
  > 
  > Wording and structure are yours; I only need the claims above to be the ones the text makes.
